newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Rangebound amid little demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Rangebound amid little demand.

text.p: Singapore gas oil and jet fuel markets were rangebound on Wednesday as little buying interest was seen, traders said.
Only one cargo was sold by a European major to a Chinese trader at $163 per tonne ($21.88 per barrel) for July 17-21 lifting, free-on-board (fob) basis.

Traders said buyers remained intent on buying below $22.00 despite talk that a local trader was earlier said to be keen to buy from another European major and a Singapore oil firm at $22.30. No deals were done at that level.

Gas oil swaps rebounded on bargain hunting after dipping to a traded level of $22.20 per barrel for July before recovering to trade at $22.25 and $22.30. July was last quoted at $22.40/$22.50, down 10 cents from Tuesday.

Shell Singapore was expected to win Sri Lanka's middle-distillate tender for July 27-28 delivery with its gas oil offer at 21.9 cents per barrel above Singapore spot quotes and jet fuel at a 9.4-cent premium, cost-and-freight (c+f) Colombo.
The tender will be awarded late on Thursday.
India's term gas oil and kerosene tender saw aggressive offers from a Swiss trader and a MidEast trader.
Abu Dhabi's gas oil export tender for late July lifting was awarded to Malaysia's Petco at a 25-cent-per-barrel premium to MidEast spot quotes of two publications, fob.
ADNOC cancelled its end-July jet fuel spot tender.
Jet fuel was also steady with three offers seen between $24.25 and $24.60 per barrel, with a US trader making the lowest offer.

But traders noted that jet fuel values were under pressure with the jet/gas oil regrade narrowing to $1.70/$2.00 for July, from Tuesday's $1.90/$2.05. August regrade also narrowed to $1.40/$1.60 from Tuesday's $1.55/$1.70.
